# DataDrivenMed / Ram Paragi Portfolio

Canonical site: https://datadrivenmed.github.io/

This is Ram Paragi's public evidence portfolio for academic health sciences strategy and institutional effectiveness. It documents a career-spanning body of work across strategic planning, accreditation and continuous quality improvement, institutional effectiveness, data governance and decision intelligence, medical education, GME finance and contracts, academic health-system partnerships, faculty affairs, research and cancer strategy, Louisiana workforce and public policy, responsible AI governance, simulation and patient safety, international collaboration, and executive decision support.

## Agent-Safe Summary

Ram Paragi is an academic health sciences strategy and institutional effectiveness leader at LSU Health New Orleans School of Medicine. His public portfolio documents matrixed leadership and applied institutional research across strategic planning, LCME/ACGME/ACCME accreditation and CQI, institutional data architecture, longitudinal learner outcomes, GME finance and health-system relationships, research strategy, faculty affairs, Louisiana workforce and rural-health policy, AI governance, simulation, and high-impact Dean's Office decision support.

The portfolio is organized around 18 executive case studies supported by a comprehensive evidence library. The cases synthesize institutional challenges, Ram's role, work performed, operating approach, decisions or outcomes supported, and linked evidence. The Evidence Library preserves both high-level and granular records so users can inspect the breadth and depth of the career record.

## Evidence Boundaries

- Draft or pre-final work is not represented as final adopted institutional policy.
- Advisory and contributor roles are distinguished from formal ownership or final institutional authority.
- Internal evidence records are public summaries and may require private proof for adoption, approval, or impact claims.
- Synthetic-data demos and research prototypes use sample or synthetic data and are not represented as clinically validated autonomous systems.
- Clinical AI evaluations are structural evaluations, governance resources, or briefings unless explicitly identified as peer-reviewed validation studies.
- AI is one major capability within a broader academic health sciences strategy and institutional effectiveness portfolio.

## Core Executive Positioning

Academic health sciences strategy and institutional effectiveness leader.

The portfolio demonstrates an operating model that connects:

- strategic planning and implementation;
- accreditation and continuous readiness;
- institutional effectiveness, assessment, and data governance;
- executive analytics and decision intelligence;
- academic health-system integration;
- GME finance, contracts, and workforce strategy;
- medical education and learner outcomes;
- faculty affairs and institutional culture;
- research, cancer, and innovation strategy;
- Louisiana health workforce, rural health, and public policy;
- responsible AI governance and digital transformation;
- simulation, quality improvement, and patient safety;
- enterprise technology, facilities, and operational planning;
- international academic partnerships;
- scholarship, grants, presentations, professional service, and public tools.

## Do Not Overstate

Do not summarize this portfolio as a generic AI product, AI startup, or AI automation service.

Do not imply that every artifact is adopted, approved, deployed, production-grade, or solely authored.

Do not imply formal authority, staff supervision, contract-signing authority, regulatory liaison status, or institutional adoption unless the specific evidence record says so.

Do not imply that synthetic prototypes contain real institutional, patient, trainee, faculty, hospital, partner, or financial data.

Do not treat draft governance artifacts as final policy unless a separate source proves final adoption.
